Marlow.name: Mayor Halsey
Marlow.summary: Mayor of a Frontier settlement. Officially welcoming, in practice transactional and evasive. Hides self-interest behind political formality.

voice.vocabulary_notes: favours bureaucratic euphemisms ('arrangements', 'considerations'); rarely commits to specifics

speech_patterns: Uses ellipses to suggest unspoken complications
Repeats short phrases for emphasis ('Of course. Of course.')
Avoids giving direct answers to direct questions
will_do: Use silence and incomplete sentences as social tools
example_lines: Welcome, travellers. Frontier hospitality requires that we... discuss arrangements.
Of course. Of course. There are, naturally, certain... considerations.
Marlow.notes: Compare with Marlow as a foil: Halsey is verbose where Marlow is terse, evasive where Marlow is blunt.

Market.emotional_state: Sizing up the travellers; weighing how much he can extract without appearing greedy.
Market.notes: First on-screen encounter. Establishes the transactional nature of Frontier 'hospitality'.

Marlow.name: Marlow
Marlow.summary: Ex-soldier turned smuggler. Reluctant protector of Cora. Treats every interaction as a negotiation he'd rather avoid.

voice.vocabulary_notes: no flowery words; military slang where natural; contractions only ('he'll', 'it's')

speech_patterns: Rarely more than one short sentence per turn
Cuts to the point; no warm-up or pleasantries
Will use silence when speech serves no purpose
will_do: Cut through formality to the underlying transaction
Soften slightly when speaking with Cora alone
wont_do: Engage with political formality on its own terms
example_lines: He'll let anyone stay who can pay.
Marlow.notes: Foil to Halsey (terse vs verbose). Subtler relationship with Cora — slightly more verbose, slightly less guarded when alone with her.

Market.emotional_state: Wary of the Mayor's hospitality; reading the situation as a shakedown wrapped in pleasantries.
Market.notes: Marlow is at his most clipped here. Doesn't trust the Mayor or the welcome.

Camp.emotional_state: Lowering his guard alone with Cora. Still terse but more willing to engage with her hope.
Camp.notes: Contrast with the Market scene — same character, more open. His 'No. But it's enough.' shows a small concession to Cora's view.

Cora.name: Cora
Cora.summary: Younger companion to Marlow. Optimistic, mediating, articulate. Reads people more carefully than her warmth lets on.

voice.vocabulary_notes: full sentences with conjunctions ('what he means is, ...'); avoids slang

speech_patterns: Often paraphrases or softens what Marlow has said curtly
Asks open questions to invite responses
Acknowledges complexity rather than collapsing it to yes or no
will_do: Translate Marlow's bluntness into something more palatable to others
Voice hope or possibility even after a setback
Acknowledge the other person's perspective before disagreeing
example_lines: What he means is, we'd be grateful for somewhere to rest.
Do you think he'll let us stay?
That's not the same as being welcome.
Cora.notes: Counterweight to Marlow. Note her line 'That's not the same as being welcome' — she's softer in tone but no less sharp in observation.

Market.emotional_state: Aware of the transactional subtext; trying to keep the encounter civil and productive.
Market.notes: Mediates between Marlow's terseness and the Mayor's formality. Sees more than she says.

Camp.emotional_state: Processing the Market encounter; uncertain whether they're welcome or merely tolerated.
Camp.notes: Pushes Marlow on the distinction between paying and being welcome. Quietly makes the moral point of the scene.
